overview: Shukla-dhyana is a state of pure meditation in Jainism, representing the highest form of concentration and spiritual purity. It is considered the pinnacle of spiritual practice and is divided into two main categories: prithakatva-vitarka-shukla-dhyana and ektva-vitarka-shukla-dhyana. These states are characterized by complete mental stability and focus, free from any form of attachment or aversion. Shukla-dhyana is essential in achieving kevala-jnana, the ultimate knowledge of liberation in Jain philosophy. This meditation is practiced by advanced spiritual aspirants and is described in detail in Jain scriptures, emphasizing the importance of detachment and the cessation of karmic influx.

primary_sources.title: Tattvartha Sutra
primary_sources.author: Umasvati
primary_sources.translation: The pure meditation (Shukla-dhyana) is of two kinds: with separate reflection and with singular reflection.
primary_sources.notes: Tattvartha Sutra is a key Jain text that outlines the path to liberation, including the stages of meditation.

misconceptions.myth: Shukla-dhyana can be easily achieved by anyone.
misconceptions.reality: In reality, Shukla-dhyana is an advanced meditative state that requires significant spiritual discipline and is typically accessible only to highly advanced practitioners.
